facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: According to Hindu mythology, Lord Vishnu rests on his serpent bed in the Ksheer Sagar from Shayani Ekadashi to Prabodhini Ekadashi.
facts.text: According to the Padma Purana, Vishnu enters into cosmic yogic sleep on Devshayani Ekadashi in the month of Ashadha and awakens four months later on Prabodhini Ekadashi in the month of Kartika.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Uttishthottishtha Govinda tyaja nidram jagatpate, tvayi supte jagannatha jagat suptam bhaved idam.
facts.text: The Bhavishya Purana details the specific awakening mantra recited on Dev Uthani Ekadashi, proclaiming that while the Lord of the universe sleeps, the entire cosmos remains asleep.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Beseeched by Brahma and the gods, Vishnu slays the demon Shankhasura who had stolen the Vedas and plunged into the ocean, restoring cosmic order.
facts.text: In the Kartika Mahatmya of the Padma Purana, Vishnu takes the Matsya avatar to kill the demon Shankhasura in the ocean and recover the Vedas before withdrawing into his four-month slumber.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: To fulfill the boon granted to the virtuous Daitya King Bali, the Lord consented to protect his threshold in Sutala.
facts.text: A popular devotional legend recounts that Vishnu agreed to dwell in the netherworld as a guardian for King Mahabali during the four monsoon months, leaving the earthly cosmos unpresided.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The Tulsi-Vivah ceremony marks the official end of Chaturmas, from which day all auspicious activities and the wedding season resume.
facts.text: The ritual performance of Tulsi Vivah on Dev Uthani Ekadashi ceremonially solemnizes the marriage of the sacred tulsi plant to Vishnu, formally marking the reopening of the Hindu wedding season.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: During this time the god Vishnu is believed to be 'sleeping,' and because of this the period is considered inauspicious for weddings and initiation.
facts.text: Puranic injunctions strictly prohibit all new rites of passage, including marriages and housewarmings, during Chaturmas because the divine preserver is resting in Yoga Nidra.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Cave 13 contains a large Anantasayana panel, which depicts a resting figure of Vishnu as Narayana, measuring 12 feet in length.
facts.text: At Cave 13 of the Udayagiri Caves near Vidisha, the Archaeological Survey of India preserves a 3.65-metre rock-cut relief panel of Vishnu reclining in yogic sleep dating to the early fifth century CE.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The magnificent panel on the southern wall of the sanctum represents Vishnu resting on the cosmic serpent Shesha in his yogic sleep.
facts.text: At the Dashavatara Temple in Deogarh, surveyed by the Archaeological Survey of India, an exterior sixth-century CE relief depicts Vishnu in cosmic sleep on the coils of Sheshanaga flanked by Lakshmi.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: On the northern wall is a magnificent and large Vishnu reclining in the Anantasayana pose atop the serpent Adisesha.
facts.text: In the seventh-century CE Mahishasuramardini Cave temple at Mamallapuram, protected by the Archaeological Survey of India, a granite relief portrays Vishnu reclining on Adisesha while the demons Madhu and Kaitabha approach.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The second level of the cave features a colossal monolithic sculpture of Lord Vishnu in a reclining posture on Adisesha.
facts.text: At the Undavalli Caves near the Krishna River, the Archaeological Survey of India protects a monolithic sandstone cave complex featuring a five-metre-long reclining sculpture of Vishnu dating to the seventh century CE.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Fasts and restrictions during this period coincided with practical necessities, as diseases spread readily and travel was halted during the heavy monsoon.
facts.source_name: History of Dharmasastra by P. V. Kane
facts.text: Historians and traditional theologians disagree on whether the marriage ban during Chaturmas was conceived as an astronomical reflection of solar Dakshinayana or as an agrarian adaptation to severe Indian monsoon rains that prevented travel and wedding feasts.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Scholars have long discussed the historical interactions between the Buddhist vassa, Jain chaturmas, and Brahminical rainy-season observances.
facts.text: Scholars debate whether the four-month stationary vow of Chaturmas originated in Vedic Brahminical domestic rituals or was adopted from the monastic rain retreats observed by early Buddhist and Jain orders.
